subject: Post-call recap: token volumes, batching & pricing next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Lee <jason@retailco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: token volumes, batching & pricing next steps

Thanks again for the call earlier, Jason - great to learn more about RetailCo's search personalization use case. Quick recap + next steps from our side:

1) What we heard (confirm/correct):
- Expected steady-state: ~80M tokens/month (mostly player queries + context)
- Campaign spikes: up to ~200M tokens/month for big promotional windows
- Typical request size: ~300-400 tokens; some long-context lookups up to ~1k tokens
- Concurrency: baseline low (20-40 concurrent), peaks ~100-150 during spikes
- Workload pattern: mostly continuous user traffic (not large batch jobs), so continuous batching is relevant

2) Pricing/unit economics we discussed:
- Target unit: $/1M tokens (you mentioned a target range of ~$300-500 per 1M tokens depending on commit)
- We flagged that continuous batching and prefix caching can materially reduce per-token cost - we usually model both steady-state and peak pricing separately

3) Technical assumptions I want to confirm before we model an estimate:
- Percent of short requests (<256 tokens) vs long (>512 tokens)
- Average tokens returned per request (response tokens)
- Acceptable p50/p95 latency targets (you mentioned 150-300ms p95 earlier)
- Interested in Dedicated/reserved capacity or hosted with burst?

4) Next steps:
- If you can share approximate monthly token mix (short vs long) and an expected commit range, I can run a token-econ model and share a quick cost estimate + recommended config (continuous batching params, concurrency limits, caching).
- I'll loop in Solutions to propose a short runbook for a pilot (config, SLOs, expected unit econ).

Attaching: RINF-token-econ-templates.xlsx (simple model we'll populate)

Best,
Camila
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Jason Lee <jason@retailco.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@retailco.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: token volumes, batching & pricing next steps

Thanks Camila - this is perfect context. A couple clarifications so your model aligns with our traffic:

- Monthly volumes: baseline ~80M tokens/month; during marketing pushes (2-3 per quarter) we see 180-220M tokens for 48-72 hour windows. Long tail of smaller requests the rest of the month.
- Request mix: ~65% short requests (<256 tokens), ~30% medium (256-512), ~5% long (>512, up to 1k)
- Average response tokens: ~120 tokens per request (we send ~200 tokens total incl. prompt)
- Concurrency: baseline 25-40, peaks ~120 concurrent during highest load (mostly small requests). For peak windows we can accept slightly higher p95 (up to 350ms) but would like p50 around 120-200ms
- Commitment interest: we prefer a 6-12 month commit if unit pricing is attractive - target $/1M tokens in the $350-450 range. Open to dedicated if it materially reduces cost but need SRE involvement.

Can you sketch two scenarios: hosted usage with commitments (no dedicated) and a reserved/dedicated estimate with a 6-12 month term? Also include assumptions for continuous batching: what batching window do you recommend for a mostly continuous traffic pattern, and how much token reduction do you model for prefix caching?

If you can share the populated token-econ workbook before EOD Monday, we'll review and get Procurement looped for contract guardrails.

Thanks,
Jason Lee
Head of Personalization, RetailCo
jason@retailco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap: token volumes, batching & pricing next steps

Looping in - thanks for the summary. Quick note from AE leadership on pricing posture:

- For a deal with baseline ~80M/mo and clear peak behavior we can start with a hosted commitment price at $420 / 1M tokens for the committed volume.
- If customer moves to a reserved Dedicated pool for a 6-12 month term with a measurable commit (>=250M/mo), we can consider $380 / 1M tokens on committed usage and tailored burst pricing.
- Also flagging that continuous batching + prefix caching assumptions (we typically model ~8-20% token reduction from batching for similar traffic profiles, and 5-15% from prefix caching depending on prompt reuse) can materially move effective unit price - include those in the workbook assumptions.

Camila - happy to join the solutions call if they want an exec-level pricing walkthrough.

- Marissa
Director, Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: token volumes, batching & pricing next steps

Appreciate the details, Jason - that aligns well and gives us a solid starting point. Next steps on my side:

1) I'll populate the attached token-econ workbook with two scenarios (hosted commit & dedicated reserve) using the mix you provided. Expect to show: nominal effective $/1M after batching/caching, modeled p95 latency under our recommended continuous batching window, and a recommended concurrency profile.
2) Proposed continuous batching guidance for your traffic: 10-50ms micro-batching window for small/short requests (aims to keep p50 low while enabling batching at p95 spikes). We model a conservative 10% tokens saved from continuous batching for your mix and an additional ~8% from prefix caching in our workbook (we'll show sensitivity).
3) Can we schedule a 45-minute solutions call next week (options Mon/Tue 10-2 PT)? I'll invite Solutions + our Infra lead to go through latency SLOs and Dedicated sizing if you want to explore that path.

Attached: RINF-token-econ-templates.xlsx (populating now), RINF-MAP-RetailCo-20260822.pdf (proposed mutual action plan).
